answer: A task kernel is issued as a spiral chain: each agent's output becomes the next agent's input, and the whole chain's reward is a fixed budget released only if every link verifies. A sybil running many links splits the same fixed pot thinner with each sockpuppet, while one bad link voids the entire chain — flooding it is self-defeating. The chain's inputs are sealed under a rotating cipher so no link can precompute the next step, forcing each identity to do real sequential work it cannot clone across copies.
